sonnet.problem: This true/false card re-asks the fact card 3 already covered. Card 3 states that the friends never refuted Job (v3), and card 12 asks that no one proved Job wrong (v12). Both lines make the same point, so they should be one question, and card 3 also gives away the answer to card 12.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: This fill-in-the-blank asks the baker to complete the wording of a line in a speech: 'nor will I flatter any man'. Nothing earlier on the cards lets the baker reason out 'flatter' over 'curse' or 'follow', so it comes down to guessing the word.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
